hook_text: Before you draw a single line, steal from the engineers who have lifted miners for a hundred years. Here is how to investigate a headgear.
clip_script: Investigation has a purpose, questions, sources and a record. Look at three to five real headgear in photographs, drawings, a visit if you can, and a talk with someone who worked on a mine. Scale the photos from a person or a bakkie: tower sixty metres, sheave five. Four parts: the winder on the surface, the wire rope, the sheave at the top turning the rope downwards, and the cage or skip. Drum winders wind rope onto a drum and sit beside a steel A-frame whose back-leg leans towards the winder house to resist the rope's pull. Friction winders grip the rope over a wheel on top of a concrete tower. Law demands brakes, catches, stops and indicators. Then steal: triangles in every face, a back-leg towards your motor, a rigid base, a real sheave, guide strings, a brake, a bumper, a pointer. Write where each came from and why.
visual_style: Photographs fan across a whiteboard table; a ruler scales a worker against a tower; the rope path animates drum to sheave to cage; an A-frame leans and a back-leg props it; a checklist of borrowed features ticks down.
pacing: Sources and scale, the four parts, two winders, three forms, the borrowed list.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find two photographs of South African headgear with a person or vehicle in them for scale.
